items.title: Geoff Bull Interview, 1966-05-05
items.q: this is a lot of the younger kids at that stage got on this kick when the Bill Haley records came out, you know, the rockers.

ctx.x: Well, I know what you mean. Yeah. Well, I don't know what you call them. Like mods and rockers in England. Yeah, yeah, that sort of thing. With that equivalent of that. Well, this is, this is, this is a lot of the younger kids at that stage got on this kick when the Bill Haley records came out, you know, the rockers.

And we weren't interested in that at all. I wasn't. So we used to go to the jazz club every Saturday night from then on and listen and so on and so. And, as I say, I'd, I'd, I'd played the bugle. Mm-hmm. And I, I'd, just around about, just before that stage, I'd, I'd managed to bully my mother into buying me a trumpet. Mm-hmm. Which I was going to learn to play and I had a few lessons on, on, on the trumpet just to sort of, you know, I started off having lessons. I didn't know I was going to stop having lessons.…
